A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark correlations, evaluation runtimes, ablations and generative-performance prediction results.

after.justification: v2 reports revised empirical results and adds a manual quality assessment of generated distractors.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the stated LL scoring component from summed sample log-likelihoods to mean character-length-normalized log-likelihoods. The benchmark reformulations, distractor-generation procedures and three-checkpoint linear regression remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, TriviaQA, SQuAD 2.0 and HumanEvalPack across the same six programming languages, with MMLU and BoolQ pairings. The new distractor audit examines existing benchmark material without expanding task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain MC, random-MC, LL, answer-only variants, MMLU, BoolQ and the additional SQuAD distractor condition. LL regression already appears in v1 Table 6; its addition to Figure 2 does not introduce a comparator.

E3.justification: The reported LL metric changes from a sum to an average with explicit character-length normalization. v2 also introduces a manual-review protocol involving one author and 50 randomly selected questions per audited benchmark. Model checkpoints, prompting settings and regression design remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 3.4 adds a distractor-quality audit of 100 questions, finding one correct distractor and eight cases with duplicate distractors. Existing reasoning-removal, cross-benchmark and distractor-count ablations remain, with revised results.

E5.justification: Both versions report one random seed for random-distractor construction and p-values alongside correlation coefficients. No additional repeated-run, confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is introduced; changed p-values are result changes.

E6.justification: Tables 3 and 7 substantially replace correlation results: LL macro Pearson correlation changes from -0.58 to 0.90 for TriviaQA and from -0.19 to 0.86 for HumanEval. Table 6 replaces GSM8K LL prediction error of 'inf' with 0.021 and HumanEval's 1.923 with 0.021. These accompany the revised LL specification and cannot be treated as demonstrated same-setting gains. MC correlations also change, while Table 5 runtimes remain identical.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the mathematical LL score definition from summed log-likelihoods to mean_i[log P(y_i|x_i)/|y_i|], specifying character length. The complexity statement in Equation 1 remains mathematically equivalent, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The conclusion broadens the main correlation claim from NLG–MC to NLG–NLU and explicitly endorses LL as a viable alternative. This materially changes the claimed usefulness of one of the two principal evaluation shortcuts. The contribution statement also changes from a planned benchmark release to a released evaluation framework.

C2.justification: Section 4 replaces the interpretation of LL as generally poor and fragile with an approximately competitive, simpler alternative. It also replaces the claimed smart-distractor advantage for larger models with no clear difference. Cross-benchmark pairing is newly qualified as exploratory, and the limitations now explicitly identify models above 7B as untested.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a project link instead of a release promise, specifies LL character normalization, and reports under 30 minutes for prompt adaptation and 16–24 hours for distractor generation, including manual checks and JSON repairs. Appendix A prompts and Table 8 checkpoint details are unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but Section 2.2 expands differentiation from Zhang et al. through LL evaluation, lightweight distractor generation, broader capabilities and consistently positive correlations. Section 3.4 also explicitly claims novelty for cross-benchmark pairing analysis.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect related work, scoring explanations, results and limitations. Cross-benchmark pairing is folded into Section 3.4, with subsequent subsection renumbering. The overall narrative structure and appendix prompts remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 has revised curves, scales and legend placement. Figure 2 adds LL and predicted-LL curves, changes axis ranges and expands its caption, displaying an analysis already evaluated in v1. Tables move with text reflow, but their overall structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit LL definition, distractor-quality audit, generation-cost disclosure and project link improve transparency and reproducibility relative to v1. These are concrete but limited gains. The PDFs do not explain the provenance of the large result replacements, so the more favorable LL findings alone do not establish a major quality improvement.
